messages:
mia_support: Heads-up — AcmeAI is seeing intermittent 429s. They have two API keys (same org) behind a NAT/proxy. One key gets 429s, the other keeps working. Can someone clarify scoping precedence (API key vs project vs org vs IP) and what exact logs/headers we need to triage?

jess_engineer: Need the raw 429 response + headers. Specifically: x-request-id, any x-rate-limit-* headers, response body, last-4 of the API key(s), project id, and the egress IP shown by the customer. Also whether they use Authorization header or rely on an API key query param.

mia_support: Provided sample from customer:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX-9f3a" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Headers:
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710001234
  X-RateLimit-Scope: org
  X-Request-ID: req_abc123def
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"org rate limit exceeded"}
They also included another request where Authorization header was present but proxied differently and that one succeeded.

rl-ratebot: [rate-limiter] Attribution summary for req_abc123def -> matched_scopes=[api_key:sk-live-XXXX, ip:34.210.11.22, org:org-987], attribution_priority=[api_key, project, org, ip], final_throttle_scope=org

sarah_sre: Looks like a fingerprinting/attribution edge-case. TL;DR: our runtime attempts to attribute to API key first, then project, then org, then IP. But if the proxy strips or rewrites Authorization or we see mismatched fingerprints (Auth header present but different from observed key propagation), the rate-limiter can fall back to org or IP attribution. We rolled out a fingerprinting heuristic that ties requests with the same TLS/connection fingerprint -> but some proxies terminate TLS and re-origin, which breaks it.

sarah_sre: Repro steps for the customer to send back so we can be definitive:
1) Capture two requests (one failing, one succeeding) and paste the full curl and full response (including raw headers).
2) Send us the X-Request-ID headers from both responses.
3) From their proxy team: confirm whether they rewrite Authorization or use header stripping, and whether they set `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`.
4) Run both variants locally (direct vs via their proxy) and include `-v` output.

sarah_sre: Quick local repro command we asked them to run (works for us):
```bash
# direct request (should attribute to API key)
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX-9f3a" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'

# proxied request (if proxy removes auth, we will see IP/org attribution)
curl -v https://proxy.theircorp.net/relay -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.210.11.22" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX-9f3a" -d '{"url":"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate","body":{}}'
```

tom_prodeng: If this repro confirms proxy is rewriting/terminating auth, short-term options: 1) ask customer to preserve Authorization and forward raw headers, 2) create a per-project key and bind it to their project so even if we attribute to project it won't hit org-level limit, or 3) move to Dedicated capacity. Long-term: we should harden attribution so API key beats IP even when fingerprinting fails. I'll create INF ticket.

mia_support: Ok will ask AcmeAI for the `-v` outputs + both X-Request-IDs. Also asked them to try per-project key. Escalating to SRE/Infra w/ initial data (INF-2793).

jess_engineer: One more ask: include timestamps and sample of their NAT table if available so we can correlate multiple customer sessions to same external IP.

mia_support: On it, sending checklist to customer now. :thumbsup:

sarah_sre: Thanks — once we get X-Request-IDs I'll pull rate-limiter traces and post back quick findings. If it's an attribution bug we can roll a config to prefer API key attribution immediately.
